wedge: K-apt public monthly common-management fees + same-complex history + comparable-complex baseline + public maintenance/work history => flag unusually large common-fee changes and explain which public line items or maintenance events are the likely drivers, without requiring a household bill, login or private utility data
last_material_result: One bounded data+action discovery unit selected a narrower apartment-fee anomaly wedge rather than another directory/reminder. The raw data layer is unusually feasible: K-apt publicly exposes complex management-fee lookup, 1:1 and 1:N comparisons, regional averages and maintenance history, while the public-data portal exposes apartment lists, basic complex metadata and common-management-fee APIs. The main substitute risk is real but not yet fatal. Apartment-i already analyzes a logged-in household bill and compares electricity/water/gas and same-complex/same-size averages, so a generic 'manage my apartment bill' product is commoditized and excluded. K-apt itself already does raw comparison, and a third-party K-apt comparison site exists. The surviving wedge is therefore public common-fee anomaly detection plus a plain-language 'what changed and why might it have changed?' explanation across months/peer complexes, available without resident authentication. This is materially different from household-bill payment/analysis and from static comparison, but one more substitute/distribution check is required before Founder Gate.
economics: KRW0 discovery spend. Data acquisition can plausibly remain free through K-apt/public-data sources and a static or periodically generated site; no user account or private bill ingestion is required. Monetization is indirect: apartment-name long-tail SEO -> ads, moving/home-service affiliate or portfolio cross-promotion. Expected contribution is unproven; viability depends on whether anomaly/explanation pages create search value beyond K-apt and existing comparison pages with low refresh burden.
next_checkpoint: Next run: validate the exact anomaly/explanation gap and distribution economics. Search for Korean services/pages that already flag month-over-month or peer-adjusted common-management-fee anomalies and explain drivers using K-apt data. Also test whether apartment-name + 관리비/관리비 상승/평균 queries expose indexable long-tail surfaces. KILL if incumbents already provide automated anomaly explanations or if generating useful explanations requires private household bills/manual investigation; advance toward BUILD Gate only if the public-data transformation remains distinct and batch-generatable at KRW0.
recommendation: KEEP at ASSESS for one more bounded substitute/distribution check. Do not build a generic management-fee comparison or household bill analyzer. Only pursue the public, no-login anomaly + likely-driver explanation wedge.
